instructions: Trim both ends of the plantains, cut a slit down the skin, and peel them. Cut them on a slant into 1/4-inch slices.
Heat the 3 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until it's hot but not smoking.
Add a single layer of slices and fry for 1 to 1 1/2 minutes, until the underside is light golden. Flip them and cook for 1 minute. Work in batches so the pan isn't crowded.
Transfer the slices to a plate lined with paper towels.
Arrange the plantains on a platter, drizzle with the 1 cup crema, and sprinkle with the 2 tbsp sugar. Serve warm.
method_notes: No fried plantains with cream recipe online shows a rating, so this leads with the Tailgater Magazine Guatemalan fried plantains (La Preferida), the only one with amounts for the crema. The Spanish Academy Antigua page has no amounts, and Growing Up Bilingual (5.0 from 2) fries thicker rounds for 2 to 3 minutes a side. The sugar is the source's optional topping. If you use plain sour cream instead of crema, thin it with a little water.
